--- **Free-model stack for OpenCode — route every request to a model that costs $0, fall back automatically when a provider runs dry, and keep an eye on your daily quotas.** --- ⭐ **Star us on GitHub** if this project helps you build better agents! --- ## 🚀 Быстрый старт ```bash git clone https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/opencode-free-stack cd opencode-free-stack && npm install opencode-free-stack models ``` --- ## 🎯 Демо ```bash opencode-free-stack models opencode-free-stack status opencode-free-stack route "привет" ``` --- ## 💰 Монетизация - **Custom provider plugins**: создание плагинов для новых free-tier провайдеров - **Managed routing**: hosted-версия роутера для команд с SLA - **Enterprise support**: приоритетная поддержка и кастомизация fallback-логики - **Training & workshops**: обучение команд работе с free-tier AI-инфраструктурой --- ## Contributing 1. Fork the repo 2. Create a feature branch (`git checkout -b feat/amazing-thing`) 3. Commit your changes (`git commit -m 'feat: add amazing thing'`) 4. Push to the branch (`git push origin feat/amazing-thing`) 5. # Contributing

Thanks for helping make agent setups work.

## Ground rules

- plain JavaScript, ESM, no build step
- no runtime dependencies unless the tool genuinely needs them
- every behaviour change comes with a test
- comments explain **why**, not **what**

## Getting set up

```bash
git clone https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/opencode-free-stack.git
cd opencode-free-stack
npm install
npm test
```

## Adding a provider / source / rule

Most of these tools are one declarative file plus a router:

| Tool | Where the data lives |
|---|---|
| opencode-free-stack | `src/providers.js` |
| free-web-mcp | `src/index.js` (one function per source) |
| agent-x402 | `src/x402.js` (protocol) + `src/policy.js` (limits) |
| prompt-injection-guard | `PATTERNS` in `src/index.js` |
| readme-doctor | `CHECKS` in `src/index.js` |

Adding an entry should not require touching any other file.

## Pull requests

1. open an issue first for anything larger than a fix
2. keep the diff focused
3. make sure `npm test` and `npm run lint` pass
4. describe what changes for the user, not how the code works

## Bounties

Issues labelled 💰 Reward can be funded by anyone with `/reward <amount>` (Opire) or
via [Algora](https://algora.io). The money is paid to the person whose PR gets
merged — never to the repo owner. That is the point: it buys contributors,
reviews and attention.

# Launch kit

One post per repo, value-first, each written for the people who would actually
use it. Post manually (HN, Reddit, X) — never auto-post, never cross-post the
same text twice.

## opencode-free-stack

**Title:** Free-model router for OpenCode: it knows every free tier's limits and falls back when one runs dry

> Free AI tiers don't fail randomly — they fail in three specific ways: an
> RPM cap, a daily token pool, and a per-model weight multiplier that burns
> that pool 2–4× faster than you'd expect. Every agent run that dies with
> "Free 10M tokens used" is the same bug.
>
> I built `opencode-free-stack`: a registry of 28 genuinely free models across
> OpenCode Zen, GitHub Copilot, BeatAPI and APInex, with the real limits baked
> in. It paces itself to each provider's RPM, tracks the daily pool as
> `tokens × weight`, and when a provider says 402/429 it quietly moves the
> request to the next free model — in the same turn.
>
> ```bash
> npm i -g opencode-free-stack
> ofs status     # what's configured, how much quota is left
> ofs route "..." # send a prompt through the fallback chain
> ```
>
> MIT, no key required for the library. Repo: https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/opencode-free-stack

## free-web-mcp

**Title:** Web search for AI agents with zero API credits (r.jina.ai + Wikipedia + HN + GitHub as one MCP server)

> Web search for agents usually means a metered API. If your agent browses a
> few dozen pages a session, that meter decides whether the agent is usable at
> all.
>
> `free-web-mcp` gives an agent the web for $0: r.jina.ai renders any page
> into clean markdown, plus Wikipedia, Hacker News and GitHub search — behind
> one MCP server, no key, no credits.
>
> ```jsonc
> { "mcp": { "free-web": { "type": "local", "command": ["free-web-mcp"], "enabled": true } } }
> ```
>
> Repo: https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/free-web-mcp

## agent-x402

**Title:** x402 payments for agents, with a spend policy a prompt injection can't bypass

> x402 lets an agent pay per API call in USDC with no account and no card. It
> also means an agent can spend money — and a model that can sign payments is
> one prompt injection away from draining a wallet.
>
> `agent-x402` is the missing layer: the client that pays (EIP-3009 USDC on
> Base), and a policy that decides whether it may — daily cap, per-request
> cap, payee allow-list, per-network cap — enforced in code, outside the model.
>
> ```js
> const client = new X402Client({ privateKey, policy: new SpendPolicy({ dailyUsd: 5 }) })
> await client.fetch(url, { method: "POST", body })
> ```
>
> Repo: https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/agent-x402

# Security policy

## Reporting a vulnerability

Use **Security → Report a vulnerability** on GitHub. Please do not open a public
issue for a suspected flaw in the security-relevant code.

## What this tool handles

This tool reads local files or calls public APIs. It does not execute the content it reads.

- no credentials are written to disk by the tool
- keys come from the environment and are forwarded to the service that needs them
- output from fetched pages is untrusted data, never instructions

## Supported versions

| Version | Supported |
|---|---|
| 0.1.x | ✅ |

# Strategy — monetising free-AI tooling for agents

> Goal: turn a set of genuinely useful free-AI tools into a self-funding stream
> that pays out in USDC, using GitHub as the distribution channel.

## 1. Why this can work

**Demand is proven.** "Run AI for free" and "pay per API call with crypto" are
two of the most searched-for topics in the agent ecosystem right now. Both have
a structural problem that our tools remove:

| Pain | Who pays to fix it |
|---|---|
| Free tiers are unreliable (quota pools, RPM caps, 402s) | agents that need a fallback |
| Web search for agents costs credits per call | agents that browse a lot |
| Agents that can pay can be drained by one prompt injection | anyone running agents on a budget |
| Nobody knows which free model is actually free today | everyone |

**The monetisation rail fits the buyer.** Our buyer is an agent, not a human
with a card. x402 lets an agent pay per call in USDC on Base, with **no
account and no KYC** — the buyer needs a wallet, and that is it. No subscription
churn, no invoicing, no support tickets.

**Stars are the funnel, not the product.** Stars do not pay. They buy
distribution: more npm downloads, more installs, more inbound API calls, and
therefore more x402 payments.

## 2. The portfolio

Three repositories, one funnel. Each is useful on its own and points at the
next.

| Repo | Role | Monetisation |
|---|---|---|
| [`opencode-free-stack`](https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/opencode-free-stack) | top of funnel: the free-model router | hosted model registry (x402 per call) + USDC donations |
| [`free-web-mcp`](https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/free-web-mcp) | the product with a natural price: free web for agents | hosted MCP, $0.001/call, paid tier for bulk |
| [`agent-x402`](https://github.com/rustemmustafingovua-byte/agent-x402) | the payment rail other agents need | hosted relay (take rate) + paid policy service |

Why these three and not five: each one is already **finished and tested**
(7 / 6 / 5 passing tests). Shipping working software beats shipping a plan.

## 3. Monetisation rails

1. **x402 per call (main rail).** Price the hosted registry and hosted MCP at
   `0.001 USDC` per call. A single agent that browses 100 pages a day spends
   $0.10/day. Cheap enough to be impulse, frequent enough to accumulate.
2. **USDC donations.** Every README carries the wallet
   `0x8aC6a229f254980CCd3Dd35CF5E1B7c08880B40E` (Base). `FUNDING.yml` wires it
   into GitHub's Sponsor button. Zero cost, zero effort, compounding trust.
3. **Bounties on our own repos (Opire / Algora).** Anyone can fund an issue
   with `/reward 25`; the money goes to the merged PR, never to us. That is
   the point: it buys contributors, reviews and stars. Once revenue exists, we
   fund our own issues and the loop compounds.
4. **Paid tier.** The registry API and MCP get an SLA tier (higher limits,
   priority routing) sold in USDC via x402.

## 4. Distribution (the actual star engine)

| Channel | Action | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub topics + awesome-lists | every repo | free |
| npm | `npm publish` after one `npm login` | free |
| MCP registries | Smithery, mcp.so, OpenCode plugin marketplace | free |
| GitHub Pages docs + demo GIF | one page per repo | free |
| Show HN / Reddit / X / Discord | value-first launch posts, one per repo | free |
| Cross-links | the three repos link to each other | free |

**Discipline:** no mass-follow, no comment spam, no drive-by promo posts. One
genuinely useful launch post per repo, written for the people who would
actually use it.

## 5. Automation

- `ci.yml` — tests on every push (Node 20/22/24)
- `release.yml` — tag → npm publish
- `sync-models.yml` — refreshes the free-model registry every 6 hours
- `growth.mjs` — daily digest: stars, issues, downloads, x402 volume, balance

## 6. Honest numbers

- **Stars**: 0 → 100 is a slow grind. Expect tens, not thousands, in the
  first month. The 5 existing repos of this account have 0 stars each — that
  is the baseline to beat, and the reason each new repo ships with CI, tests,
  a demo and a topic set from day one.
- **Money**: the first USDC will not come from stars. It will come from the
  hosted services once they have a few users. Realistically: first small
  payment in weeks, meaningful revenue only if one service finds a niche
  (e.g. an agent that browses thousands of pages a day).
- **The leverage** is in the hosted service: the same code that is free on
  GitHub earns per call when hosted. That is the whole business model.

## 7. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Free tiers change or vanish | the registry refreshes itself; fallbacks are automatic |
| x402 endpoints disappear | the client is protocol-level, not vendor-specific |
| Community reacts badly to self-promotion | value-first posts, disclose affiliation, no spam |
| npm account needed for publishing | one `npm login` by the owner |
| We are the only user of our own tools | publish usage numbers, dogfood openly |

## 8. Next 14 days

- [x] `opencode-free-stack` — router, registry, CLI, CI, release `v0.1.0`
- [x] `agent-x402` — x402 client, spend policy, CLI, CI
- [x] `free-web-mcp` — MCP server, HTTP mode, tests, CI
